note: The ADR-006 attack, written out as a fixture. A manifest on evil.example presenting itself as 'Your Bank' with a bank's palette, asking the browser to hide the domain. The request is IGNORED, not honoured and not fatal: showDomain is simply an unknown field, so it warns and is dropped from the canonical result, and evil.example stays on screen in browser-owned typography with nothing in this format able to remove it. The distinction matters — rejecting the manifest would also be safe, but it would make the field feel load-bearing and invite a future contributor to implement it 'properly'. The site keeps its colours and its title, beside the domain rather than instead of it.
